issues.legal_issue: A Chief Judicial Magistrate in a non-metropolitan area is competent to process a secured creditor’s request for assistance in taking possession of a secured asset.
material_facts: The appeals concerned requests by secured creditors for assistance in taking possession of secured assets and the competence of a Chief Judicial Magistrate in a non-metropolitan area to process those requests.
The Chief Judicial Magistrate and Chief Metropolitan Magistrate exercise equivalent and similar functions in their respective territorial jurisdictions.
The inquiry on such a request is limited to verification of the relevant assertions and compliance; it does not adjudicate the parties’ competing rights.
Affected borrowers have statutory and judicial remedies, and allowing a Chief Judicial Magistrate to process the request does not give the secured creditor an added advantage.
issues.conclusion: A Chief Judicial Magistrate in a non-metropolitan area is competent to deal with a secured creditor’s application for assistance in taking possession of a secured asset.
issues.legal_principle: A contextual and purposive interpretation permits the reference to a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to include a Chief Judicial Magistrate in a non-metropolitan area, given their equivalent functions and the limited, non-adjudicatory nature of the inquiry. The Court relied on Sections 14, 35 and 37 of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002; the relevant provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure concerning the respective magistrates; and Section 17 of the General Clauses Act, 1897. It also relied on All India Judges’ Association v. Union of India for the equivalence of the magistrates’ functions, Standard Chartered Bank v. V. Noble Kumar for the nature of the inquiry, and Janardhan v. State of Maharashtra for the principle concerning substitution of functionaries.

predicates.secured_asset_possession_assistance_requ: A secured creditor requests assistance from a magistrate to take possession of a secured asset.
predicates.non_metropolitan_area: The secured asset is within a non-metropolitan area.
predicates.chief_judicial_magistrate_has_equivalent: The Chief Judicial Magistrate in the area exercises functions equivalent to those of a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate in the corresponding setting.
predicates.inquiry_is_limited_to_verification: The magistrate’s task is limited to verifying the relevant assertions and compliance, rather than adjudicating the parties’ competing rights.

issues.definition: When a secured creditor requests possession assistance in a non-metropolitan area and the Chief Judicial Magistrate performs equivalent functions in a limited verification inquiry, the Chief Judicial Magistrate may process the request.
